Interface Injector

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
public interface Injector extends AutoCloseable
The user-facing entry point for obtaining instances and providers.

Each create() (or builder() Injector.Builder.build()) call produces a fresh, independent graph: its singletons are created once within that injector and are not shared with any other injector. Discard an injector to discard its singletons.

Prefer constructor injection: annotate a single constructor with @Inject so a bean's dependencies are final, explicit, and available the moment it is constructed. Field and method injection exist for cases constructor injection cannot reach (e.g. framework-managed or cyclic wiring) and leave a window where the bean is only partly initialised.

The injector itself is injectable: any bean may declare an Injector (or Provider<Injector>) dependency and receives the injector that built it. Injector, Context, and Factory can never be bound.

    • scopedChildBuilder

      Injector.ChildBuilder scopedChildBuilder(Class<? extends Annotation> scope)
      Returns a builder for a child of this injector that hosts the child-local scope: its bindings layer over this injector's graph, and it builds and caches the instances of scope's beans resolved through it or its descendants.

      A scoping annotation is child-local when no Scope service handles it. Each bean of such a scope is created once per hosting child, built through that child, and cached there. Resolving it through an injector with no hosting child in its chain fails with a ScopeResolutionException. Hosting children nest: the nearest one in the chain hosts the bean.

      Parameters:
      scope - the child-local scope the child hosts
      Returns:
      a builder for a child of this injector that hosts scope

    • close

      void close()
      Closes this injector: rejects further resolution through it, including through the providers it returned, closes its live child injectors, newest first, then invokes @PreDestroy on every scoped instance it created, in reverse creation order. A child injector's scoped instances are those of the scope it hosts. When a callback or a child fails, the others still run, and the first failure is thrown with the later ones suppressed. Closing a child never closes its parent. Idempotent.
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
